text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.N. envoy arrives on Cyprus aiming at a high-level summit with letters and a few ideas.
- Labour dispute looms at Cyprus Airways. Stewards warn of work stoppage unless 120 seasonal staff members are given permanent jobs.
- New Cyprus Airways boss gets tough with unions.
- Boss of the Cyprus Broadcasting Corporation pledges to balance the books by 2001.
- The National Council will convene more often after criticism by communist Akel that it meets only after the presidency takes decisions.

- President Clerides' hands are untied after the national council meeting. Deliberate vagueness in what Cyprus considers "common ground" for talks to resume with the Turkish Cypriots leaves room for flexibility.
- Commercial banks are breaking the law, charging up to 2 percentage points more on their loans, on which the legal interest rate is 8.5 percent.
